_comments: MJ: Actions — the three collections that replace MJActionEntityExtended's hand-written getters.
Those getters were memoized filters over ActionEngineBase's preloaded caches, which is exactly
Source 'cache' + Load 'lazy': fill on first read, from RAM, zero queries.
ReadOnly is left to its default (true, because Source is cache), so the records handed out ARE
the engine's own instances — same as the getters did — and the collection itself refuses
Add/Remove/Clear, contributes nothing to a save, and never reports dirty.
OnRemove is therefore absent: a read-only collection has no removal semantics.

_comments: MJ: AI Agents — three collections, one of which is self-referential and needs care.
Prompts: AgentID is NOT NULL and ExecutionOrder is genuinely positional (which prompt runs
first), so it gets the Sequence policy. From is 0 because the column defaults to 0, not 1.
Source 'database' and ReadOnly false are the defaults, but they are stated explicitly here
because this is the ONE writable collection among the eight — leaving them implicit makes it
read as an oversight next to its cache/lazy siblings, and it is the opposite.
Actions: AgentID is NULLABLE on this junction, but OnRemove is still 'delete' — an
AIAgentAction row with a null AgentID is not a valid detached record, it is garbage.
SubAgents: OnRemove is 'orphan', NOT 'delete'. ParentID is nullable, and detaching a
sub-agent should demote it to a root agent — deleting it would destroy an entire agent
together with its own prompts, actions and run history because someone reorganised a
hierarchy. No Sequence policy either: renumbering ExecutionOrder here would rewrite the
agent records themselves, so the column is used for ordering only.
NOTE: MJ: AI Agents has a SECOND self-relationship (DefaultCoAgentID) which is deliberately
NOT declared — hence RelatedEntityJoinField in every lookup below, which is what keeps these
two rows apart.

_comments: MJ: AI Prompts -> MJ: AI Prompt Models. PromptID is NOT NULL, Hard delete.
Deliberately NO Sequence policy despite Priority being an integer: Priority is a SEMANTIC
ranking (which model to prefer), not a positional line number. Auto-renumbering it on every
save would silently rewrite a deliberate preference — a sequence policy suits line numbers,
not rankings. OrderBy alone gives the read ordering without touching the values.

_comments: MJ: API Keys -> MJ: API Key Scopes. APIKeyID is NOT NULL, Hard delete. Priority is a
ranking, so no Sequence policy (same reasoning as AI Prompt Models above).
BEHAVIOUR CHANGE WORTH KNOWING: MJAPIKeyScopeEntityServer overrides ValidateAsync to check
the scope's row filter, and that override is governed by DefaultSkipAsyncValidation — which
defaults to true, so today it is effectively dead. Companion validation runs each child's
ValidateAsync UNCONDITIONALLY, so declaring this collection turns that check on for every
scope on every API Key save. That is the intended rollup and a security-relevant improvement,
but a pre-existing malformed row filter will start failing saves.
